**⚡ Quick safety checklist for your Lovable + Supabase + Stripe launch**

⚠️ Your app is an **Amber**‑level project (logins, personal data, payments).  
Below are one‑sentence actions you should do *before* posting on Product Hunt.

| What to check | Why it matters | How to do it (a quick click or two) |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Ship‑check & secret scan** | Ensures no keys are in the client, no accidental public data, and that your Stripe/ Supabase secrets are in secrets or a `.env` file (not visible in the repo). | `python3 scripts/check_secrets.py ./ --report ship‑report.md` (runs locally if you can, or <https://github.com/MAL4/seatbelt> has a quick‑start). |
| **2. Supabase RLS & grants** | Every table must allow only the user who owns the row to read/write. | In Supabase UI → *Database* → *Tables* → *RLS* → enable + add 「authenticated」 policy for `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the tables you use. |
| **3. Stripe webhook verification** | The “paid” / “subscription” status must come from Stripe’s signed webhook, not from a front‑end button. | In your server code (edge, serverless, or backend) add `Stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` and only grant access after a successful check. |
| **4. Billing alerts & spending caps** | Stripe, Supabase, and any paid AI (OpenAI, Cohere, etc.) can spend unexpectedly. | Stripe → *Billing* → set a monthly budget + email alert. Supabase → *Billing* → enable “Auto‑stop” at free tier or set a limit. For any AI, add a user‑level counter in your DB and stop after X requests/month. |
| **5. Email sender set‑up** | The default “magic-link” email from Supabase is throttled (few mails/hour). | Connect a real SMTP provider (SendGrid, Mailgun, etc.) in Supabase Auth settings. |
| **6. Review privacy notice** | You’re collecting emails, possibly payment data. A short privacy statement and link is required. | Create a /privacy page with: “We store only what you give us… we don’t share data… you can delete your account at any time.” |
| **7. “Delete my account” flow** | Users must be able to remove themselves; the server must anonymise or delete rows and files. | Add a `/delete‑account` endpoint that deletes user rows (or sets a `deleted_at` flag) and calls Supabase storage API to remove their bucket files. |
| **8. Test two user logins** | Verify that user A cannot see user B’s data (rows, bucket files). | Sign up as two dummy accounts, then in the public “stranger” test mode (or with a small script) check isolation. |
| **9. Quick sanity test** | Run the app locally → sign‑up → buy a test subscription → cancel → delete account. | `npm run dev` → open → follow the flow → note any console errors. |

### One‑screen plan (you can copy‑paste into `PROJECT.md` or keep here)

```
What we are building: Lovable app with Supabase Auth and Stripe payments.
Who uses it: Public users who want to sign in, buy a plan, and store data.
Risk level: Amber (logins, personal data, payments).

Day‑one features: 1. Sign‑up / login with email magic link 2. Stripe checkout for a monthly plan 3. Dashboard showing user‑only data

Information stored: User email, payment status, personal data (e.g. profile picture). All private.

Logins: Email‑only magic link, via Supabase Auth.
Payments: Stripe Checkout, webhook validation, monthly quarterly billing.

Built with: Lovable (Vue‑like components), Supabase (Postgres + auth + storage), Stripe (API keys in secrets).

Steps:
1. Run ship‑check (see above). ✔️
2. Confirm RLS & grants in Supabase. ✔️
3. Add webhook validation in server code. ✔️
4. Connect a real SMTP provider. ✔️
5. Set Stripe billing alert. ✔️
6. Add /privacy page. ✔️
7. Implement delete‑account endpoint. ✔️
8. Test two user isolation. ✔️
9. Run full flow locally, note any errors. ✔️

Safety: Secrets never in frontend, RLS on all tables, spending caps on Stripe and AI, database back‑ups, save points before each change.
Not in version one: social login, external data fetching, AI chatbots, analytics dashboards.
```

> **Next step:**  
> 1. Run the local script to check secrets (`check_secrets.py`).  
> 2. If it passes, open your Supabase dashboard and enable RLS on every table, adding a policy like  
> `allow SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE where auth.uid() = user_id`.  
> 3. In your server code, add the webhook verification snippet (link to the Stripe docs).  

Let me know when you’ve finished a step or if you hit a hurdle. Happy launching!
